what_happened: Verified ai/init.lua's safe_require loader-acceptance claim by executing the exact validation logic headlessly against the planned sapience-plugin.lua spec table (and a stt-plugin.lua control), upgrading the seed report's code-trace-only finding to an executed test. Also read snacks.win/snacks.terminal source directly to confirm position/size key behavior rather than inferring it.

snacks.win applies size fractions uniformly to height/width, but a split consumes only one of them while a float consumes both -- so mapping a single 'size' option onto both win.height and win.width is safe for bottom/left/right but produces an unintentionally square window for position=float unless the plan explicitly decides between accepting the square float or falling back to the style default 0.9/0.9 for float. Left as an open decision for the plan (see report 02's Recommendation 4).

Two research passes left zero mechanical unknowns for the plan: snacks.win position/size semantics, loader acceptance, the free keymap suffix, and the git-root idiom were all pre-verified, so plan authoring only had to settle three genuine design choices (float sizing, ai/README.md subdirectory entry, set_position live-reposition) rather than re-derive facts.

First draft of the plan cited real suite names from suite_selection_select in two Tier Justifications, but validate-artifact.sh flagged both as fabricated: the selector aggregates across ALL of a phase's touched paths, and one path per phase (sapience-plugin.lua, docs/MAPPINGS.md) returns __FULL_SWEEP__, making the whole phase a sentinel case. Fixed by switching both to the sub-case (c) --only-gate 4 form. Lesson: run the selector over the phase's full path set, not per path.

Phase 1 terminal.lua: the plan's own dependency-constraint comment text ('neotex.*') collided with the plan's grep-based verification for the same constraint (grep -n 'neotex\.' ...). Reworded the comment to say 'the neotex namespace' instead, keeping the no-require constraint satisfied by construction and the grep clean.

Phase 6 full-gate run (bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh, no --skip-slow/--only-gate) failed 5 of 43 checks: gate 8 (run-all.sh, 9 failing suites: test-double-loading-check.sh, test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh [EXPECTED], test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh, test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, test-orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh [EXPECTED], test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh), gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep exceeded its 60s timeout under heavy concurrent system load), gate 20 (eager-load total 68606B exceeds recorded baseline 66800B), gate 22 (shellcheck findings in lint-routing-wiring.sh, test-routing-resolution.sh, lean-plan-compliance-check.sh), gate 24 (dead-command-recommendation lint: /ide references in memory-setup.md and memory-troubleshooting.md). All five are core-extension/.claude infrastructure findings with zero overlap with this task's touched paths (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/sapience/*, sapience-plugin.lua, ai/init.lua, keymaps.lua, which-key.lua, ai/README.md, docs/MAPPINGS.md) -- none mention sf1, sapience, or any Lua file. This matches the dispatch context's own flagged pre-existing core-extension deploy staleness. Re-ran gate 8's run-all.sh in isolation after confirming the first run's gate-lock (held by an earlier, self-aborted verify-deploy.sh attempt, pid 3024704) had released; the 9 failing suites reproduced identically, confirming they are not lock-contention artifacts. Not repaired here per the plan's explicit scope (a redeploy is whole-tree regeneration, outside this plan).
